page: The Vultr vx1-g-32c-128g-1920s is a general-purpose server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical AMD EPYC cores running at 2.0 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and is bundled with 1920 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 vector extensions, AVX_VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier status in stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and PassMark memory scores. Large-block memory write bandwidth also ranks in the top 10%. Multi-core scaling is moderate, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core scores, and software compilation speeds landing in the average tier. For language model workloads, the system delivers top-tier text generation speeds on small and medium models, though prompt processing speeds for larger models remain average.

From a resource density perspective, the server offers a balanced ratio of compute to memory alongside high-capacity local NVMe storage, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring fast local disk access without the premium of memory-optimized instances. The primary tradeoff lies in its moderate multi-core CPU scaling relative to its high single-core capabilities. This profile is suitable for database operations, static web serving, redis key-value stores, and text-processing pipelines.
